sources.entry: A search engine) is an information retrieval system designed to help find information stored on a computer system. This includes Web search engines.

summary.name: Information retrieval
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing information retrieval (IR), the field of computing that finds and ranks stored documents, data and metadata relevant to a search query.
use_cases: understanding how search engines rank results
learning information retrieval models and terminology
finding evaluation metrics for search systems
summary.what_it_does: The article defines information retrieval as identifying and returning resources relevant to an information need, typically expressed as a query. It explains that IR systems rank results by a numeric match score rather than returning exact matches as SQL does. It covers model types (set-theoretic, algebraic, probabilistic, feature-based) and the sparse, dense and hybrid classification of modern neural models. It also gives a timeline from punch-card systems and early online databases through PageRank, BERT, MS MARCO, ColBERT and SPLADE, plus a list of major conferences.
notable: Covers the sparse, dense and hybrid taxonomy of modern retrieval models
Detailed timeline from punch-card systems (1801) to BERT and SPLADE
Explains ranking versus exact-match database querying
caveats: Encyclopedia article, not a software tool; the Wikipedia page itself carries a note that it needs more citations
Some sections are sparse or contain unresolved clarification tags
